# ValidaThor ⚡️

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/README.md

# ValidaThor ⚡️

⚠️ This library is still under active development ⚠️

Inspired by the likes of [Zod](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod) and [Valibot](https://github.com/fabian-hiller/valibot).

## Roadmap

This is a very short-term roadmap mind you and nothing here is final

- [x] ⚙️ Setup build system and package the library
- [x] 📚 Add some basic documentation
- [x] 🧬 Improve TypeScript types

## Example

```tsx
import * as v from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Define your schema shape
const exampleSchema = v.object({
  name: v.string([v.min(2)]),
  age: v.number([v.min(13), v.max(100)]),
  email: v.string([v.email()]),
  avatar: v.object({
    path: v.string(),
    size: v.number(),
  }),
  acceptedTerms: v.boolean(),
  createdAt: v.date([
    v.min(new Date('2021/01/01')),
    v.max(new Date()),
  ]),
  tags: v.array(v.string())
});

// If the input data matches the schema, nothing will happen,
// Otherwise an error will be thrown to help the user
try {
  v.parse(
    exampleSchema,
    {
      name: 'John Doe',
      age: 35,
      email: 'email@example.com',
      avatar: {
        path: 'https://placekeanu.com/200/200',
        size: 2048
      },
      acceptedTerms: true,
      createdAt: new Date('01/08/2023'),
      tags: ['tag1', 'tag2', 'tag3']
    }
  );
} catch(err) {
  // Do something with the error
};
```

Made by [Kevin Østerkilde](https://oesterkilde.dk/?utm_campaign=validathor&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme)

# Parse core function

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/core/parse.mdx

# Parse core function

The `parse()` core function is used to parse your schema and input data, and then run all the validations on your fields.

It's exported as a separate function which you can use, but it's also important to know that each schema provides a `parse()` function by itself - See the example below.

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { parse } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const mySchema = object({ ... });

parse(mySchema, { ... });
// Or
mySchema.parse({ ... });
```

---

# ValidateModifiers core function

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/core/validate-modifiers.mdx

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# ValidateModifiers core function

<Callout type="info" emoji="ℹ️">
  This function is *primarily* for internal use.
</Callout>

Some schemas accept modifiers, such as `min()` or `email()` which can modify the way a schema works.
`validateModifiers()` is a function used within these schemas to validate this array of modifiers easily, rather than checking them one by one in the code.

It's exposed in the library, though I've yet to find a use for it myself in external code.

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { min, max } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';
import { validateModifiers } from '@nordic-ui/validathor/core/validateModifiers';

const numberModifiers = [min(2), max(12)];

validateModifiers(4, numberModifiers);
```

# ValidaThor ⚡️

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/index.mdx

# ValidaThor ⚡️
 
What exactly is it? It's a **super simple**, validation library!

Define the shape of your data using our schemas and modifiers, and match it against your data for easy validation.

## Getting started

```sh npm2yarn
npm i @nordic-ui/validathor
```

import { Tabs, Tab } from 'nextra/components'

## Example

Here's a basic example usecase

<Tabs items={['Schema', 'Usage #1', 'Usage #2']}>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
    import * as v from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

    // Define the shape of your schema
    // Make use of modifiers in places where it makes sense
    const exampleSchema = v.object({
      name: v.string([v.min(2)]),
      age: v.number([v.min(13), v.max(100)]),
      email: v.string([v.email()]),
      avatar: v.object({
        path: v.string(),
        size: v.number([v.min(0)]),
      }),
      acceptedTerms: v.boolean(),
      createdAt: v.date([
        v.min(new Date('2021/01/01')),
        v.max(new Date()),
      ]),
    });
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
    // If the input data matches the schema, nothing will happen,
    // Otherwise an error will be thrown to help the user
    try {
      exampleSchema.parse({
        name: 'John Doe',
        age: 35,
        email: 'email@example.com',
        avatar: {
          path: 'https://placekeanu.com/200/200',
          size: 2048
        },
        acceptedTerms: true,
        createdAt: new Date('01/08/2023')
      })
    } catch(err) {
      // Do something with the error
    };
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
    import * as v from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

    // If the input data matches the schema, nothing will happen,
    // Otherwise an error will be thrown to help the user
    try {
      v.parse(
        exampleSchema,
        {
          name: 'John Doe',
          age: 35,
          email: 'email@example.com',
          avatar: {
            path: 'https://placekeanu.com/200/200',
            size: 2048
          },
          acceptedTerms: true,
          createdAt: new Date('01/08/2023')
        }
      );
    } catch(err) {
      // Do something with the error
    };
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

# Credit Card modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/creditCard.mdx

# Credit Card modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string is a valid credit card number using the Luhn algorithm.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { creditCard, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const creditCardRule = string([
  creditCard({
    type_error: "Must be a valid credit card number",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = creditCardRule.parse('4111 1111 1111 1111');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Validation Details

The credit card modifier:
- Accepts card numbers with or without spaces and dashes
- Validates using the Luhn algorithm (mod 10 check)
- Accepts card numbers between 13 and 19 digits
- Does not perform card type detection

## Supported Card Formats

The modifier accepts credit card numbers from all major card issuers:

- **Visa**: 13 or 16 digits, starting with 4
- **Mastercard**: 16 digits, starting with 51-55 or 2221-2720
- **American Express**: 15 digits, starting with 34 or 37
- **Discover**: 16 digits, starting with 6011, 622126-622925, 644-649, or 65
- **JCB**: 16 digits, starting with 3528-3589

The validation accepts numbers with spaces or dashes as separators:
- `4111111111111111`
- `4111 1111 1111 1111`
- `4111-1111-1111-1111`

---

# Custom modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/custom.mdx

# Custom modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a a custom assertion is true.

If you have specific needs that are not met by existing modifiers, the `custom` modifier could be something to reach for. It works with all of the primary schema types, except `object`.

## Schemas

- `boolean`: [Learn more](/schemas/boolean)
- `date`: [Learn more](/schemas/date)
- `number`: [Learn more](/schemas/number)
- `regex`: [Learn more](/schemas/regex)
- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)
- `array`: [Learn more](/schemas/array)

## Arguments

- `assertions` - A tuple consisting of an assertion and the related error

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { custom, string, ValidationError } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const customRule = string([custom((value) =>
  [[value.toLowerCase() === value, new ValidationError('Lowercase only')]]
)]);

try {
  const parsedValue = customRule.parse('only_lowercase_chars');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

# Email modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/email.mdx

# Email modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string is an email.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `domain?` - The domain that the email should end with
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { email, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const emailRule = string([
  email("@google.com", {
    domain_error: "Not a permitted email domain",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = emailRule.parse('johndoe@example.test');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

# Ends With modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/endsWith.mdx

# Ends With modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string ends with a specific suffix.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `suffix` - The suffix that the string must end with
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { endsWith, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const endsWithRule = string([
  endsWith('.com', {
    suffix_error: "Must end with .com",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = endsWithRule.parse('example.com');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Validation Details

The endsWith modifier:
- Performs case-sensitive suffix matching
- Can check for any string suffix, not just single characters
- Returns the original string if validation passes

## Common Use Cases

```ts showLineNumbers
import { endsWith, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Validate file extensions
const imageRule = string([
  endsWith('.png', {
    suffix_error: "Must be a PNG file",
  }),
]);

// Check domain endings
const commercialDomainRule = string([
  endsWith('.com'),
]);

// Validate file types
const documentRule = string([
  endsWith('.pdf', {
    suffix_error: "Must be a PDF document",
  }),
]);

// Ensure specific formats
const percentageRule = string([
  endsWith('%', {
    suffix_error: "Must end with %",
  }),
]);
```

# Enumerator modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/enumerator.mdx

# Enumerator modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given value is one of the allowed values in the provided list.

## Schemas

- `number`: [Learn more](/schemas/number)
- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)
- `date`: [Learn more](/schemas/date)

## Arguments

- `input` - The array of values or TypeScript enum which the input value must be one of
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

import { Tabs, Tab } from 'nextra/components'

<Tabs items={['Number Array', 'String Array', 'Date Array', 'String Enum', 'Numeric Enum']}>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { enumerator, number } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      const schema = number([enumerator([0, 25, 50, 75, 100])]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse(75);
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
      ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { enumerator, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      const schema = string([enumerator(['Red', 'Green', 'Blue'])]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse('Green');
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { enumerator, date } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      const schema = date([enumerator([new Date('2024/01/01'), new Date('2025/01/01')])]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse(new Date('2024/12/31'));
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { enumerator, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      enum Color {
        Red = 'red',
        Green = 'green',
        Blue = 'blue'
      }

      const schema = string([enumerator(Color)]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse(Color.Red); // 'red'
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
      ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { enumerator, number } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      enum Status {
        Inactive,  // 0
        Active,    // 1
        Pending    // 2
      }

      const schema = number([enumerator(Status)]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse(Status.Active); // 1
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
      ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

# Includes modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/includes.mdx

# Includes modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string includes a specific substring.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `substring` - The substring that must be present in the string
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { includes, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const includesRule = string([
  includes('@', {
    include_error: "Must contain @ symbol",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = includesRule.parse('user@example.com');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Validation Details

The includes modifier:
- Performs case-sensitive substring matching
- Can check for any substring, not just single characters
- Returns the original string if validation passes

## Common Use Cases

```ts showLineNumbers
import { includes, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Ensure email-like format
const emailLikeRule = string([
  includes('@'),
  includes('.'),
]);

// Validate file extensions
const markdownRule = string([
  includes('.md', {
    include_error: "Must be a markdown file",
  }),
]);

// Check for required keywords
const licenseRule = string([
  includes('MIT License', {
    include_error: "Must contain MIT License text",
  }),
]);

// Multiple required substrings
const urlRule = string([
  includes('https://'),
  includes('.com'),
]);
```

# IP modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/ip.mdx

# IP modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string is a valid IP address.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `version?` - Optional version specification: `'v4'` for IPv4 only, `'v6'` for IPv6 only, or undefined for both
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { ip, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Accept both IPv4 and IPv6
const ipRule = string([
  ip(undefined, {
    type_error: "Must be a valid IP address",
  }),
]);

// IPv4 only
const ipv4Rule = string([
  ip('v4', {
    type_error: "Must be a valid IPv4 address",
  }),
]);

// IPv6 only
const ipv6Rule = string([
  ip('v6', {
    type_error: "Must be a valid IPv6 address",
  }),
]);

try {
  const ipv4 = ipv4Rule.parse('192.168.1.1');
  const ipv6 = ipv6Rule.parse('2001:db8::8a2e:370:7334');
  console.log('IPv4:', ipv4);
  console.log('IPv6:', ipv6);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Supported Formats

### IPv4 Addresses
- Standard dotted decimal notation: `192.168.1.1`
- All valid ranges (0-255 per octet): `10.0.0.0`, `172.16.0.1`, `8.8.8.8`

### IPv6 Addresses
- Full notation: `2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334`
- Compressed notation: `2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334`
- Loopback: `::1`
- Unspecified: `::`
- IPv4-mapped IPv6: `::ffff:192.168.1.1`

---

# Max modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/max.mdx

# Max modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given value is less or equal to the given input.

## Schemas

- `number`: [Learn more](/schemas/number)
- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)
- `date`: [Learn more](/schemas/date)
- `array`: [Learn more](/schemas/array)

## Arguments

- `max` - The maximum value that the input value must meet or exceed
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

import { Tabs, Tab } from 'nextra/components'

<Tabs items={['Number', 'String', 'Date', 'Array']}>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { max, number } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      const schema = number([max(10)]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse(4);
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
      ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { max, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      const schema = string([max(6)]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse('hello');
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { max, date } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      const schema = date([max(new Date('2026-03-24'))]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse(new Date('2024-05-10'));
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
      import { max, array } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

      const schema = array([max(3)]);

      try {
        const parsedValue = schema.parse([1, 2]);
        console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
      }
      ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

# Pattern modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/pattern.mdx

# Pattern modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string matches a regular expression pattern.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `regex` - The regular expression pattern to match against
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { pattern, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const patternRule = string([
  pattern(/^[A-Z][a-z]+$/, {
    pattern_error: "Must start with uppercase followed by lowercase letters",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = patternRule.parse('Hello');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Regular Expression Support

The pattern modifier supports all JavaScript regular expression features:

### Flags
- `i` - Case insensitive matching
- `g` - Global matching (finds all matches)
- `m` - Multiline mode
- `s` - Dot matches newlines
- `u` - Unicode mode
- `y` - Sticky mode

### Common Patterns

```ts showLineNumbers
import { pattern, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Alphanumeric only
const alphanumericRule = string([
  pattern(/^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/),
]);

// Email validation
const emailRule = string([
  pattern(/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/),
]);

// Phone number (US format)
const phoneRule = string([
  pattern(/^\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}$/),
]);

// ISO date format
const dateRule = string([
  pattern(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/),
]);

// Hex color
const hexColorRule = string([
  pattern(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
]);

// Strong password
const passwordRule = string([
  pattern(
    /^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[@$!%*?&])[A-Za-z\d@$!%*?&]{8,}$/,
    { pattern_error: "Password must contain uppercase, lowercase, number and special character" }
  ),
]);

// Semantic version
const semverRule = string([
  pattern(/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/),
]);

// URL slug
const slugRule = string([
  pattern(/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/),
]);
```

## Complex Validation Examples

```ts showLineNumbers
import { pattern, string, min, max } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Username validation
const usernameRule = string([
  min(3),
  max(20),
  pattern(/^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$/, {
    pattern_error: "Username can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores",
  }),
]);

// GitHub repository name
const repoNameRule = string([
  pattern(/^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/, {
    pattern_error: "Repository name can only contain letters, numbers, dots, hyphens, and underscores",
  }),
]);

// Credit card CVV
const cvvRule = string([
  pattern(/^\d{3,4}$/, {
    pattern_error: "CVV must be 3 or 4 digits",
  }),
]);

// Time format (24-hour)
const timeRule = string([
  pattern(/^([01]\d|2[0-3]):([0-5]\d)$/, {
    pattern_error: "Time must be in HH:MM format (24-hour)",
  }),
]);
```

## Tips

- Use the `^` and `$` anchors to match the entire string
- Escape special regex characters with backslash: `\.`, `\*`, `\+`, etc.
- Use character classes for common patterns: `\d` (digits), `\w` (word characters), `\s` (whitespace)
- Test your regex patterns thoroughly with various inputs
- Consider using more specific modifiers (like `email()`, `url()`, `uuid()`) when available

---

# Phone modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/phone.mdx

# Phone modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string is a valid phone number.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { phone, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const phoneRule = string([
  phone({
    type_error: "Must be a valid phone number",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = phoneRule.parse('+1-555-123-4567');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Supported Phone Formats

The phone modifier supports various international and domestic phone number formats:

### US Formats
- `+1-555-123-4567`
- `1-555-123-4567`
- `555-123-4567`
- `(555) 123-4567`
- `555.123.4567`
- `5551234567`

### International Formats
- `+44 20 7946 0958` (UK)
- `+33 1 42 86 82 00` (France)
- `+49 30 12345678` (Germany)
- `+81 3-1234-5678` (Japan)
- `+86 10 1234 5678` (China)

The validator accepts numbers with spaces, dots, hyphens, and parentheses as separators.

---

# Slug modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/slug.mdx

# Slug modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string is a valid slug (URL-friendly identifier).

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { slug, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const slugRule = string([
  slug({
    type_error: "Must be a valid slug",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = slugRule.parse('my-awesome-blog-post');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Validation Rules

A valid slug must:
- Contain only lowercase letters (a-z)
- Contain only numbers (0-9)
- Use hyphens (-) as separators
- Not start or end with a hyphen
- Not contain consecutive hyphens
- Not contain spaces or special characters

## Valid Examples

- `hello`
- `hello-world`
- `my-awesome-post`
- `product-123`
- `version-2`
- `a-b-c-d-e`

## Invalid Examples

- `Hello` (uppercase letters)
- `hello world` (spaces)
- `hello_world` (underscores)
- `hello.world` (dots)
- `-hello` (starts with hyphen)
- `hello-` (ends with hyphen)
- `hello--world` (consecutive hyphens)

## Common Use Cases

```ts showLineNumbers
import { slug, string, min, max } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Username validation
const usernameRule = string([
  slug(),
  min(3),
  max(30),
]);

// URL segment validation
const urlSegmentRule = string([
  slug({
    type_error: "URL segment must be lowercase with hyphens only",
  }),
]);

// Blog post ID validation
const postIdRule = string([
  slug(),
  max(100),
]);
```

---

# Starts With modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/startsWith.mdx

# Starts With modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string starts with a specific prefix.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `prefix` - The prefix that the string must start with
- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { startsWith, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const startsWithRule = string([
  startsWith('https://', {
    prefix_error: "Must start with https://",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = startsWithRule.parse('https://example.com');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Validation Details

The startsWith modifier:
- Performs case-sensitive prefix matching
- Can check for any string prefix, not just single characters
- Returns the original string if validation passes

## Common Use Cases

```ts showLineNumbers
import { startsWith, string, url } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Ensure secure URLs
const secureUrlRule = string([
  startsWith('https://'),
  url(),
]);

// Validate file paths
const absolutePathRule = string([
  startsWith('/', {
    prefix_error: "Must be an absolute path",
  }),
]);

// Check for specific prefixes
const phoneWithCountryRule = string([
  startsWith('+', {
    prefix_error: "Must include country code",
  }),
]);

// Validate namespaced keys
const configKeyRule = string([
  startsWith('app.config.', {
    prefix_error: "Must be a config key",
  }),
]);
```

# Trim modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/trim.mdx

# Trim modifier

A modifier which creates a transformation rule to trim whitespace from the beginning and end of a string.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { trim, string, min } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const trimmedRule = string([
  trim({
    type_error: "Must be a string",
  }),
  min(1), // Ensure non-empty after trimming
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = trimmedRule.parse('  hello world  ');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue); // "hello world"
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Transformation Details

The trim modifier:
- Removes all leading whitespace characters
- Removes all trailing whitespace characters
- Preserves internal whitespace
- Works with all Unicode whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, newlines, etc.)

## Common Use Cases

```ts showLineNumbers
import { trim, string, email } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Clean user input before validation
const emailRule = string([
  trim(),
  email(),
]);

// Ensure non-empty strings after trimming
const requiredTextRule = string([
  trim(),
  min(1, { min_error: "This field is required" }),
]);

// Process form inputs
const result = emailRule.parse('  user@example.com  '); // "user@example.com"
```

---

# URL modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/url.mdx

# URL modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string is a valid URL.

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { url, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const urlRule = string([
  url({
    type_error: "Must be a valid URL",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = urlRule.parse('https://example.com');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Valid URL Formats

The URL modifier uses the built-in JavaScript `URL` constructor for validation, which accepts:

- `https://example.com`
- `http://example.com`
- `ftp://files.example.com`
- `https://example.com:8080`
- `https://subdomain.example.com`
- `https://example.com/path/to/resource`
- `https://example.com?query=value`
- `https://example.com#anchor`
- `https://user:pass@example.com`

# UUID modifier

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/modifiers/uuid.mdx

# UUID modifier

A modifier which creates a validation rule to ensure that a given string is a valid UUID (Universally Unique Identifier).

## Schemas

- `string`: [Learn more](/schemas/string)

## Arguments

- `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { uuid, string } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const uuidRule = string([
  uuid({
    type_error: "Must be a valid UUID",
  }),
]);

try {
  const parsedValue = uuidRule.parse('123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Supported UUID Versions

The UUID modifier validates UUIDs according to RFC 4122, supporting:

- Version 1 (timestamp-based)
- Version 2 (DCE Security)
- Version 3 (namespace name-based, MD5)
- Version 4 (random)
- Version 5 (namespace name-based, SHA-1)

The validation is case-insensitive, accepting both uppercase and lowercase UUIDs.

# Array schema

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/schemas/array.mdx

# Array schema

A function which creates a parsing rule to ensure that a given value is an array.

## Arguments

1. `schema` - A single schema or an array of schemas
2. `modifiers?` - A list of modifiers
    - `min`: [Learn more](/modifiers/min)
    - `max`: [Learn more](/modifiers/max)
    - `custom`: [Learn more](/modifiers/custom)
3. `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Examples

```ts showLineNumbers
import { array, string, number } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const arrayRule = array([string(), number()]);

try {
  const parsedValue = arrayRule.parse(['Hello', 'world', 42]);
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## TypeScript

To get the type of a schema, you can do the following:

```ts showLineNumbers
const arrayRule = array([string(), number()]);

type ArraySchema = ReturnType<typeof arrayRule.parse>; // (string | number)[]
```

# Enum schema

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/schemas/enum.mdx

# Enum schema

A function which creates a parsing rule to ensure that a given value is one of the allowed values from an array or TypeScript enum.

## Arguments

1. `values` - An array of values or TypeScript enum
2. `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Examples

import { Tabs, Tab } from 'nextra/components'

<Tabs items={['Array Values', 'TypeScript String Enum', 'TypeScript Numeric Enum', 'Mixed Enum']}>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
    import { enum_ } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

    const colorRule = enum_(['red', 'green', 'blue'] as const);

    try {
      const parsedValue = colorRule.parse('red');
      console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
    import { enum_ } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

    enum Color {
      Red = 'red',
      Green = 'green',
      Blue = 'blue'
    }

    const colorRule = enum_(Color);

    try {
      const parsedValue = colorRule.parse('red');
      console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
    import { enum_ } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

    enum Status {
      Inactive,  // 0
      Active,    // 1
      Pending    // 2
    }

    const statusRule = enum_(Status);

    try {
      const parsedValue = statusRule.parse(1); // Active
      console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
    ```ts showLineNumbers
    import { enum_ } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

    enum UserRole {
      Admin = 'admin',
      User = 1,
      Guest = 'guest'
    }

    const roleRule = enum_(UserRole);

    try {
      const parsedValue = roleRule.parse('admin');
      console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## TypeScript

To get the type of a schema, you can do the following:

<Tabs items={['Array Values', 'TypeScript String Enum', 'TypeScript Numeric Enum']}>
  <Tab>
  As you can see here, using readonly arrays give better type safety.
  ```ts showLineNumbers
  const colorRule = enum_(['red', 'green', 'blue']);
  const permissionRule = enum_(['read', 'write', 'admin'] as const);

  type ColorSchema = ReturnType<typeof colorRule.parse>; // string
  type PermissionSchema = ReturnType<typeof permissionRule.parse>; // 'read' | 'write' | 'admin'
  ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  ```ts showLineNumbers
  enum Color {
    Red = 'red',
    Green = 'green',
    Blue = 'blue'
  }

  const colorRule = enum_(Color);

  type ColorSchema = ReturnType<typeof colorRule.parse>; // Color
  ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab>
  Using numeric enums do something odd with the return type.
  ```ts showLineNumbers
  enum Status {
    Inactive,  // 0
    Active,    // 1
    Pending    // 2
  }

  const statusRule = enum_(Status);

  type StatusSchema = ReturnType<typeof statusRule.parse>; // string | Status
  ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

# Optional schema

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/schemas/optional.mdx

# Optional schema

A function which creates a parsing rule that makes any schema optional, allowing it to accept `undefined` values.

## Arguments

1. `schema` - Any parser schema to make optional

## Examples

```ts showLineNumbers
import { optional, string, object, number } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Basic usage
const optionalString = optional(string());

try {
  const value1 = optionalString.parse(undefined); // Returns undefined
  const value2 = optionalString.parse('hello');   // Returns 'hello'
  console.log('Values:', value1, value2);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}

// With object schemas
const userSchema = object({
  name: string(),
  age: optional(number()),
  email: optional(string([email()]))
});

try {
  const user = userSchema.parse({
    name: 'John Doe',
    age: undefined,
    // email is omitted entirely
  });
  console.log('User:', user); // { name: 'John Doe', age: undefined, email: undefined }
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## Advanced usage

The optional schema can wrap any other schema, including complex nested structures:

```ts showLineNumbers
import { optional, object, array, string, min } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

// Complex nested structure
const addressSchema = object({
  street: string([min(5)]),
  city: string(),
  country: string()
});

const userSchema = object({
  name: string(),
  addresses: optional(array(addressSchema))
});

// Valid with addresses
const user1 = userSchema.parse({
  name: 'John',
  addresses: [
    { street: '123 Main St', city: 'New York', country: 'USA' }
  ]
});

// Valid without addresses
const user2 = userSchema.parse({
  name: 'Jane',
  addresses: undefined
});

// Also valid - field omitted entirely
const user3 = userSchema.parse({
  name: 'Bob'
});
```

## TypeScript

To get the type of an optional schema, you can do the following:

```ts showLineNumbers
const optionalString = optional(string());
const optionalUser = optional(object({ name: string(), age: number() }));

type OptionalString = ReturnType<typeof optionalString.parse>; // string | undefined
type OptionalUser = ReturnType<typeof optionalUser.parse>;     // { name: string; age: number } | undefined
```

## Important notes

- The optional schema only accepts `undefined` values, not `null`
- When used in object schemas, omitted fields will be set to `undefined`
- The wrapped schema's validation rules still apply when a non-undefined value is provided

---

# Tuple schema

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/schemas/tuple.mdx

# Tuple schema

A function which creates a parsing rule to ensure that a given value is a tuple.

## Arguments

1. `schemas` - A tuple of schemas
2. `message?` - A custom object with error messages to be displayed when validation fails or there are type errors

## Examples

```ts showLineNumbers
import { tuple, string, number } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

const tupleRule = tuple([string(), number()]);

try {
  const parsedValue = tupleRule.parse(['Hello', 123]);
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## TypeScript

To get the type of a schema, you can do the following:

```ts showLineNumbers
const tupleRule = tuple([string(), number()]);

type TupleSchema = ReturnType<typeof tupleRule.parse>; // [string, number]
```

---

# Union schema

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/schemas/union.mdx

# Union schema

A function which creates a parsing rule to ensure that a given unknown value matches one of the provided schemas.

## Arguments

1. `schemas` - An array of parser schemas to try in order
2. `message?` - An object with a custom error message for type mismatches

## Examples

```ts showLineNumbers
import { union, string, number, parse } from '@nordic-ui/validathor'

const unionRule = union([string(), number()])

try {
  const parsedValue = unionRule.parse('Hello world');
  console.log('Parsed value:', parsedValue);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Parsing failed:', error.message);
}
```

## TypeScript

To get the type of a schema, you can do the following:

```ts showLineNumbers
const unionRule = union([string(), number(), boolean()]);

type UnionSchema = ReturnType<typeof unionRule.parse>; // string | number | boolean
```

---

# Assert utility

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/utils/assert.mdx

# Assert utility

`assert` is used to check that a condition is truthy, otherwise it'll throw either a `ValidationError` or a custom error type.

This function is used within each of our schemas and modifiers

## Arguments

- `condition` - The condition to check
- `message?` - The error message to throw if the condition is false

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { assert } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

assert(isAdmin === true, 'You must be an admin to perform this action');
// Or
assert(typeof 123 === 'string', new TypeError('Expected a string'));
```

---

# Errors utility

Source: https://github.com/nordic-ui/validathor/blob/main/apps/docs/pages/utils/errors.mdx

# Errors utility

Out of the box, `validathor` ships with two custom error types.

These are used internally but could be useful for example to test that the right error type is thrown in your own code.

## Arguments

- `message?` - A custom error message to be displayed
- `cause?` - The original error that caused this type error. If not provided, a generic error with the default message will be set as the cause

## Example

```ts showLineNumbers
import { ValidationError, TypeError } from '@nordic-ui/validathor';

throw new ValidationError('Maximum length must be a positive number');
throw new TypeError('Expected a number');
```
